rows.title: CT GOP says medical leave program holds too much money
rows.standfirst: State officials say the family and medical leave program needs a financial safety net, but CT Republicans say it’s gotten out of hand.

rows.title: Push for CT child tax credit gains momentum
rows.standfirst: Advocates for a CT child tax credit already have enough support, at least on paper, to send a bill to Gov. Ned Lamont’s desk.

rows.title: CT pension investments increase 14%, $8.3 billion gain in 2025
rows.standfirst: Connecticut’s pension fund assets gained roughly $8.3 billion for retirement programs for state employees, teachers and others last year.

rows.title: Lamont floats possible gas tax holiday to offset price jumps
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont said he could discuss suspending CT’s 25-cents-per-gallon retail levy on regular gasoline and its 48.9-cent diesel tax.

rows.title: Lamont strikes deals with 10 unions, but many raises still overdue
rows.standfirst: Most of CT’s 35 bargaining units are overdue for raises, and time is running out for Gov. Ned Lamont to settle with a key part of his base.

rows.title: House Dems would trim rebate program to aid local schools
rows.standfirst: A plan to send local school districts $100 million to $150 million could cut into Gov. Ned Lamont’s proposed tax rebate.

rows.title: CT gas tax holiday proposal is stuck in first gear
rows.standfirst: While CT officials have spoken in support of a gas tax holiday, they also haven’t met to discuss anything and remain focused on other plans.

rows.title: Funds for signature pre-K endowment in peril as surplus dwindles
rows.standfirst: CT’s Early Childhood Education Endowment is projected to receive less than a tenth of what lawmakers pledged last June.

rows.title: Lamont flirts with his first CT budget deficit
rows.standfirst: Lawmakers built a $309 million cushion into the budget, but eroding revenues, rising Medicaid expenses and other issues wiped out most of it.

rows.title: Ritter sees compromise on CT tax rebates and aid to schools
rows.standfirst: A one-year advance on property tax credits could help CT legislators maintain or increase rebates while finding extra money for schools.

rows.title: As most states’ reserves have dwindled, CT’s safety net has grown
rows.standfirst: Connecticut has bucked a national trend, building unprecedented safeguards against a recession and federal budget cuts, a new report says.

rows.title: CT House Republicans say a one-time tax rebate is not enough
rows.standfirst: House Republicans called for the maximum property tax credit to grow to $650, which would cost CT an estimated $275 million per year.

rows.title: Finance panel endorses nearly $900M in tax-cutting options
rows.standfirst: A key CT panel endorsed nearly $900 million in new relief options, including relief for renters and expanded breaks for shoppers and seniors.

rows.title: Legislature’s $29B spending plan sets up negotiations with Lamont
rows.standfirst: The Appropriations Committee’s $29 billion budget would enhance Medicaid payments and invest in public transit, municipal grants and more.

rows.title: CT finance panel keeps Lamont tax rebate plan in play
rows.standfirst: The finance panel endorsed a 1.75% surcharge on the capital gains earnings of single filers with annual income that exceeds $1 million.
